message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; 1.00794 u for the most abundant isotope) | | **Isotopes** | • ¹H (protium, 99.98 %)
• ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %)
• ³H (tritium, trace, radioactive) | | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Molecular form** | Diatomic (H₂) under normal conditions | | **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.4 K) | | **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) | | **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.00008988 kg m⁻³) | | **Color** | Colorless | | **Odor** | Odorless | | **Taste** | Tasteless | | **Solubility in water** | ~0.0016 g 100 mL at 25 °C (very low) | | **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many non‑metals; reacts violently with oxygen to produce water (exothermic). | | **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (range 4–75 % by volume). | | **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H⁺ in solution) and a weak base (forming H⁻ in hydrides). | | **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | | **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series in UV/visible/IR; prominent 21 cm line in radio astronomy. | | **Applications** | • Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells)
• Chemical feedstock (ammonia, methanol)
• Metallurgy (reducing agent)
• Space propulsion (liquid hydrogen)
• Scientific research (spectroscopy, plasma physics) | --- ### Quick Takeaways 1. **Lightest element** – only one proton (and usually one electron). 2. **Diatomic gas** – exists as H₂ under standard conditions. 3. **Highly reactive** – readily forms compounds with almost all other elements. 4. **Low density** – lighter than air; rises quickly. 5. **Energy‑dense** – high specific energy (~120 MJ kg⁻¹) but low volumetric energy at STP. 6. **Isotopic variants** – deuterium used in nuclear fusion research; tritium is radioactive and used in nuclear weapons and fusion experiments.
